profile.what: Constellation Brands holds the exclusive right to sell Modelo, Corona and Pacifico beer in the United States, and owns a smaller portfolio of premium wines and spirits.
profile.money: Beer provides nearly all the profit. It is brewed in Mexico at the company's own breweries and sold through independent US distributors.
profile.valued: Constellation is valued on forward P/E and free cash flow on adjusted earnings, since reported profit has been hit by write-downs. The multiple depends on beer volumes.

summary.sentence: The owner of America's leading imported beers, with a record of costly side bets.
strengths: Free cash flow has been positive every year in the record.
Gross margin above half of sales.
risks: Reported losses in three of the last five fiscal years after write-downs.
Debt is larger than shareholders' equity.

meaning.what_it_does: Brews and sells Modelo, Corona and Pacifico beer in the United States under a perpetual licence, and owns a smaller wine and spirits business.
meaning.how_it_makes_money: Beer brewed in its own Mexican breweries and sold through US distributors, plus premium wine and spirits.
meaning.how_it_keeps_making_money: Its Mexican beers have taken share in the US for years and are brewed at large, efficient plants.
meaning.how_it_could_stop: Tariffs on Mexican imports, weaker spending by Hispanic consumers, or a general decline in drinking.

moat.summary: Exclusive US rights to the leading imported beer brands, including the best-selling beer in the country.

industry.summary: Beer changes slowly, though younger adults are drinking less alcohol.

management.summary: The beer business has been run well, but large write-downs on cannabis and wine investments have destroyed value.

financial_health.ratio_gaps: Not available from the data source, so not shown: a ten-year record, inventory and receivables turnover, the quick ratio, goodwill and tangible book value, and maintenance capex split from growth capex. Owner earnings therefore deduct all capex, which is conservative.

valuation.method: Fair value is the average of two methods: (1) Owner cash flow, capex held at depreciation: $2.2B a year: operating cash flow less depreciation and stock-based pay (median of the last three fiscal years and TTM). Capex is running at 2.0x depreciation, so most of it is expansion, not upkeep. (2) Damodaran: cash flow to the firm: Sales grow 1–7% for five years, fading to 3%; operating margin held at 33%; cost of capital 7.7%. Cash added, debt subtracted. The owner cash flow method grows the cash for five years, then at half that rate, 3% after year ten, discounted at 10%. Stock-based pay is deducted because it is a real cost to owners.
